root_cause.text: The `sip_help_tcp()` function in the netfilter SIP connection tracking module stores the `unsigned long` return value of `simple_strtoul()` into an `unsigned int` variable (`clen`), leading to integer truncation on 64-bit systems when parsing large SIP Content-Length headers, and lacks a check to ensure the parsed length does not exceed the TCP payload length.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff changes the declaration of `clen` from `unsigned int` to `unsigned long` and adds the validation check `if (clen > datalen) break;` to prevent processing out-of-bounds Content-Length values.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a boundary check to prevent out-of-bounds parsing when the SIP Content-Length exceeds the actual packet data length.
intent_record.what: Inserts a boundary check `if (clen > datalen) break;` before processing the SIP message body in `sip_help_tcp`.
intent_record.how: It prevents the parser from reading past the end of the received packet data when the declared Content-Length (`clen`) is larger than the actual available data (`datalen`).

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the `sip_help_tcp()` function which contains the vulnerability. Specifically, `clen` is declared as an `unsigned int` on line 1373 (`unsigned int matchoff, matchlen, clen;`) but is assigned the `unsigned long` return value of `simple_strtoul()` on line 1405 (`clen = simple_strtoul(dptr + matchoff, (char **)&end, 10);`), leading to integer truncation on 64-bit systems. Additionally, there is no check to ensure that `clen` does not exceed the remaining TCP payload length (`datalen`) before performing pointer arithmetic on line 1415 (`end += strlen("\r\n\r\n") + clen;`).
